snippet.title: This Is Why You Can't Fold Paper Forever!
snippet.description:
Think you can fold a sheet of paper forever? Think again! 🤯 In this Quirble, we're diving into the mind-bending math behind one of the most famous challenges: folding a piece of paper.

You've probably heard that it's impossible to fold a paper more than 7 or 8 times. But why? With each fold, the paper's thickness doubles, and it grows exponentially. At a certain point, the energy required to make just one more fold would be **more than all the energy in the universe!**

It's a perfect example of how simple physics and math can make an everyday action seem impossible.

Were you surprised by this scientific fact? Tell us in the comments below! 👇

Since it's made of iron, the Eiffel Tower **expands** by several centimeters in the scorching summer heat and **contracts** back down in the chilly winter cold. It's a colossal, real-world example of thermal expansion right in front of our eyes! Plus, its tip can even sway slightly in the wind.

This is a truly mind-blowing scientific fact about one of the world's most famous structures!
